items.title: Man drowns after falling into fish pond
items.summary: Kedah Fire and Rescue Department Zone 2 chief Senior Fire Superintendent II Mohd Naim Matt Jaaffar said they received an emergency call regarding the incident at 5.46pm yesterday. He said a team of seven personnel from the Guar Chempedak Fire and Rescue Station, led by Senior Fire Officer II Zayati Muda, was dispatched to the scene. The operation was assisted by a team from the Sungai Petani Fire and Rescue Station, the Padang Lembu Volunteer Fire Brigade, police, and the Health Ministry.

items.title: Kuching banker gets seven years’ jail, 16 lashes after draining client accounts via DuitNow
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 3 — A relationship manager with an international bank was yesterday sentenced to seven years’ jail, fined RM40 million and ordered to receive 16 strokes of the cane by the Sessions Court here after pleading guilty to fraud and money laundering charges. For each of the eight money laundering charges, he was sentenced to three years’ jail, with the terms to run concurrently from today, fined RM5 million or four months’ jail in default. Kho failed to pay the fine.

items.title: UNICEF estimates 20 million children suffered online sexual abuse in one year
items.summary: GENEVA: About 20 million internet-using children across 21 countries were subjected to sexual exploitation or abuse on digital platforms in a single year, with most cases occurring on social media, according to a new report by Unicef. The report estimated that more than one in five children aged 12 to 17 surveyed across Africa, Asia, Latin America and Eastern Europe experienced at least one form of sexual abuse or exploitation online in the year before they were surveyed. Roughly 15 million children in the countries surveyed were exposed to unwanted sexual content, 9 million were pressured into sexual conversations or sharing sexual images, and 4 million had sexual images shared without their consent, the report found.

items.title: Victoria Bridge incident: Father speaks on losing youngest son a year after eldest daughter
items.summary: The victim’s father, who wished to be known only as Abd Halim, 42, said his eldest daughter was only 16 when she died last year, following a four-month battle with an illness doctors were unable to diagnose. He said the family was still coping with the loss of their eldest daughter when tragedy struck again with the death of Abdul Rafee, three. “Just last year, we lost our eldest child.

items.title: 'My husband should come home today' — Hani appeals on 10th wedding anniversary
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: "My husband should come home today. He promised to bring home an anniversary present." Instead of celebrating the occasion together, Hani is waiting for news of Loe.

items.title: Shooting injures two police officers, others in Minneapolis
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Several people were shot Wednesday, including two police officers in the northern US city of Minneapolis, officials said. "The Minneapolis Police Department is on the scene of a shooting... involving multiple victims, including two police officers," the city said in a statement. Governor Tim Walz asked the public to "pray for Minnesota," while FBI Director Kash Patel said his agents were responding.

items.title: Stepfather arrested over alleged rape, sexual assault of 13-year-old girl in Besut
items.summary: BESUT: Police have detained a 40-year-old man to assist in investigations involving the rape and sexual assault of his 13-year-old stepdaughter. Deputy district police chief Deputy Superintendent Md Sani Md Salleh said police received a report regarding the case earlier yesterday. "The case is being investigated under Section 376(3) of the Penal Code and Section 14(d) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017," he said in a statement yesterday.

items.title: SDEB refutes viral claims of Sungai Johor Bridge closure, says safe to cross despite vessel strike
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept — The Sungai Johor Bridge here is safe for all road users, according to Senai-Desaru Expressway Berhad (SDEB). In a statement, SDEB said it had taken immediate action by conducting inspections and assessments of the bridge’s structural condition, following the incident of a vessel that drifted close to the bridge around 2.30 pm yesterday. SDEB said that it always prioritises safety aspects and will continue to monitor the condition of the bridge structure from time to time to ensure the safety of highway users.

items.title: TGS TW quits as auditor for 10 Bursa firms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Audit firm TGS TW PLT has resigned as external auditor for at least 10 companies listed on Bursa Malaysia across the Main, ACE and LEAP Markets, in a sweeping move that comes just months after regulatory penalties were imposed on two of the firm's partners. As of July 31, the Securities Commission Malaysia's (SC) register listed five registered individual auditors attached to TGS TW, namely, Lian Jat Meang, Lim Ge Ru, Tan Lea Ling, Tan Tian Wooi and Teoh Chey Yeat. The latest resignations come after the Audit Oversight Board (AOB) of the SC imposed sanctions on two individual auditors from TGS TQ on June 23, 2026.

items.title: Woman seeks help to verify if rescued man is missing Malaysian climber
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian woman has appealed for help to verify whether a man pictured among those rescued from the Nepal flood disaster is her missing younger brother. "The first picture looks like my brother. My brother is Zaki," she wrote.

items.title: Mercy Malaysia deploys team to Nepal as 2.2 million tonnes of debris hamper aid to flood-hit communities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — Mercy Malaysia has deployed a humanitarian team to Nepal to assess urgent needs following the catastrophic flash flood that struck the Bhote Koshi river system on Aug 26, with the team set to focus on search and rescue, emergency shelter, food, clean water and sanitation as millions of tonnes of debris hamper access to affected communities. Mercy Malaysia said its team will assess the situation on the ground, engage with affected communities and local partners, and identify the most urgent humanitarian needs. Roads and bridges have been destroyed or blocked by massive quantities of debris, making access to affected communities increasingly difficult.

items.title: Girlfriend dies in hospital after alleged beating, man held
items.summary: PENAMPANG: A 41-year-old man has been arrested following the death of his girlfriend, who was allegedly beaten after a dispute between them. District police chief Superintendent Sammy Newton said following the incident, the Penampang Criminal Investigation Department (CID) launched an investigation and subsequently detained the local man. Sammy said the Penampang CID, in collaboration with the Forensic Division (D10) of the Sabah police headquarters CID, also inspected the scene of the incident.

items.title: DOE steps up patrols amid worsening haze crisis, warns landowners against open burning
items.summary: Elaborating further, Rosli said that motor vehicle movements also generally contribute to the decline in air quality. A total of 16 stations recorded unhealthy API readings, with Bintulu, Sarawak recording the highest at 192, followed by Kapit, Sarawak (190), Kota Kinabalu Polytechnic, Sabah (178), Keningau, Sabah (175), and Kota Kinabalu, Sabah (173). Also recording unhealthy readings were Labuan (173), Samalaju, Sarawak (172), Kimanis, Sabah (171), ILP Miri, Sarawak (170), Limbang, Sarawak (169), Miri, Sarawak (166), Johan Setia, Selangor (159), Putrajaya (151), Nilai, Negeri Sembilan (151), Sandakan, Sabah (136), and Seremban, Negeri Sembilan (109).

items.title: Ringgit opens higher against US dollar ahead of OPR decision
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Thursday as investors awaited Bank Negara Malaysia's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) decision on the overnight policy rate (OPR) later today. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the focus today would be on the MPC's OPR decision, with the central bank widely expected to keep the policy rate unchanged at 2.75 per cent. Meanwhile, Mohd Afzanizam said the US Dollar Index fell 0.12 per cent to 99.555 points ahead of the US nonfarm payrolls data due on Friday.

items.title: IMF's Georgieva says rising bond yields threaten progress on developing country debt
items.summary: ASHEVILLE, North Carolina: Ballooning debt and rising bond yields in advanced economies are threatening to undo developing and low-income countries' progress in reining in their own debts, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva told Reuters. "This is not just a low-income developing countries problem," Georgieva said. "High debt levels in advanced economies, combined with stubborn inflation, could lead to debt service costs going up for everybody, including for the low income, for the emerging markets and developing economies."

items.title: PKR youth chief warns overspending could undermine country's finances
items.summary: Johan said the ministry's actual expenditure in 2023 amounted to RM1.8 billion compared with its approved allocation of RM1.1 billion, while in 2024, expenditure reached RM2 billion against an allocation of RM1.3 billion. The overspending continued in 2025, with actual expenditure touching RM2.3 billion against an approved allocation of RM1.6 billion. For 2026, the approved allocation was RM2.1 billion, with actual expenditure already hitting RM1.9 billion as of June.

items.title: 'Dangerous behaviour': FAA fines Boeing US$3.1mil over safety violations
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Boeing paid a US$3.1 million fine to the US Federal Aviation Administration this year, after the agency said the planemaker had committed a series of safety violations, including actions tied to the 2024 Alaska Airlines MAX 9 mid-air emergency, the FAA told Reuters Wednesday. The FAA said the full amount sought in September 2025 was paid by Boeing in January and had not been previously disclosed publicly. Boeing also confirmed to Reuters it paid the fine.

items.title: New York bans AI use for students until high school
items.summary: New York bans AI use for students until high school AFP NEW YORK: New York is banning student use of artificial intelligence until high school, the city's mayor announced Wednesday, in a move designed to protect children's education and mental health. The one-year restriction, which impacts nearly 600,000 public school pupils through eighth grade, will be closely watched across the United States as the city's school board is by far the largest in the country. Only high school students – typically aged 14 and above – will be permitted to use artificial intelligence in limited pilot programs, and they will be offered biannual AI literacy classes.

items.title: Gold rebounds over 1pct as US dollar, yields pull back from highs
items.summary: NEW YORK: Gold bounced from a near one-month low on Wednesday as the US dollar and Treasury yields retreated from recent highs, while investors awaited US payrolls data due later this week for cues on the Federal Reserve's policy path. Spot gold rose 1.1 per cent to US$4,376.41 an ounce by 01:57 p.m. EDT (1757 GMT), rebounding from its lowest level since Aug 7 hit earlier in the session. US gold futures for December delivery edged 0.4 per cent higher to settle at US$4,414.60.

items.title: Oil settles 1pct higher, as US-Iran strikes threaten supplies
items.summary: HOUSTON: Brent crude prices settled one per cent higher in a volatile session on Wednesday, driven by renewed military strikes between the United States (US) and Iran that have restricted world oil supply. US forces struck Iran's southern coast and Iran fired on American bases across the region. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures rose 79 cents, or 0.9 per cent, to settle at US$91.01.

items.title: Japan bond yield surge puts ringgit in the spotlight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Japan's bond market is becoming a competitor for global capital again, raising the prospect of money flowing back to the country and putting pressure on the ringgit and Malaysian assets, analysts said. The concern comes after Japan's benchmark 10-year government bond yield breached three per cent on Tuesday for the first time since 1996, offering domestic investors returns rarely seen in decades. SPI Asset Management managing director Stephen Innes said yields at that level could give Japanese institutions greater reason to keep capital at home or repatriate some funds invested overseas.

items.title: Why internal audit fails
items.summary: Internal audit is intended to provide independent assurance, identify risks, evaluate controls and help organisations improve governance and performance. The problem is often not the existence of internal audit but how internal audit is positioned, managed and executed. Internal auditors must be sufficiently independent from the activities they audit.

items.title: Oil rush adds RM590mil to Hengyuan's market value in two days
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hengyuan Refining Company Bhd has added about RM590 million to its market value in just two trading days, emerging as the biggest winner from a renewed rush into oil and gas stocks. The refiner's shares have jumped 99 sen, or 50.77 per cent, from RM1.95 last Friday to RM2.94 at Wednesday's close, lifting its market capitalisation from about RM1.17 billion to RM1.76 billion. When trading resumed on Tuesday, Hengyuan hit its daily limit, soaring 58 sen, or 29.74 per cent, to RM2.53 as investors piled into energy counters amid renewed hostilities between the United States (US) and Iran.

items.title: Wall Street ends higher as stocks reclaim some shine
items.summary: All three major US stock indexes gained ground, with the small-cap Russell 2000 outperforming its larger-cap peers, rising 1.1 per cent. Nvidia, the chipmaker at the forefront of the AI wave, rose 3.2 per cent, while Micron and Qualcomm gained 2.4 per cent and 2.0 per cent, respectively. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 295.01 points, or 0.56 per cent, to 53,061.89, the S&P 500 gained 35.16 points, or 0.46 per cent, to 7,666.63 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 118.05 points, or 0.45 per cent, to 26,217.83.

items.title: Trump 'happy' Prince Harry and Meghan have left US
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump said Wednesday he was glad Prince Harry and Meghan Markle had left the United States – though adding that if he were part of the British royal family he would not have taken them back. "I thought they treated the royal family with great disrespect. I wouldn't have taken him back, right?

items.title: ADI equips workers with industry-ready skills - HR Ministry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Workplace-based training is gaining ground among businesses, with 1,366 companies,including 677 small and medium enterprises (SMEs), now participating in the government's Academy in Industry (ADI) programme. He said the programme combined classroom learning with workplace training, enabling participants to familiarise themselves with actual company technology, systems and processes. ADI uses two main approaches, namely ADI Apprenticeship and ADI Employment.

items.title: ADI helps companies turn experienced workers into future leaders
items.summary: The company joined the government's Academy in Industry (ADI) programme to upskill its workforce, allowing employees to strengthen their competencies in their existing roles Schott Glass Malaysia human resources manager Suhaila Mustapha Kamal said this was particularly valuable for workers who already had operational experience but needed to strengthen their competencies before moving into bigger roles. Building on what they know Suhaila said about 80 per cent of their ADI programme involved workplace activities, with the remaining 20 per cent focused on theory. The programme also incorporates training within industry elements, including job instruction, job methods, job relations and problem solving.

items.title: BUDI95 fuel quota back to 300 litres: How will this affect motorists?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — Five months after reducing the monthly subsidised RON95 quota from 300 litres to 200 litres, the government has restored the higher limit. But with government data showing average monthly RON95 consumption is around 100 litres, what does the restored litres mean for current consumers? A motorist who uses 100 litres a month will still purchase only 100 litres.

items.title: 5,000 Dropbox accounts hacked
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: Dropbox said on Tuesday around 5,000 accounts were compromised last month, with hackers viewing and downloading content stored on the cloud-storage platform. Hackers accessed files in fewer than a third of the compromised accounts, the company said. Lenovo identified a "legacy integration" between Lenovo ID and Dropbox that "could be used to improperly authenticate certain Dropbox accounts".

items.title: Black bass rediscovered in Penang
items.summary: The Penang Fisheries Department said the catch was significant as local fishermen had not reported seeing the species in the state for about 15 years. Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) ichthyologist Associate Professor Dr Khaironizam Md Zain said the finding was significant for another reason as well — Penang lies considerably outside the species' previously known distribution. Khaironizam said further sampling and surveys were needed to determine whether the species had established a resident population in Penang.

items.title: Maltese tycoon acquitted of masterminding reporter's murder
items.summary: VALETTA: A Maltese court on Wednesday acquitted tycoon Yorgen Fenech of orchestrating the brutal murder in 2017 of investigative reporter Daphne Caruana Galizia, which brought down a government and drew global condemnation. The wealthy businessman had stood accused of masterminding the car-bomb killing of 53-year-old Caruana Galizia. Caruana Galizia's family said in a statement that Fenech's acquittal was "denying her the justice she deserves."

items.title: Sabah is safe for travel, US tells foreign tourists
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The United States is encouraging its citizens as well as people in other countries to travel to Sabah. US Embassy Chargé d'Affaires to Malaysia David Gamble said this followed improvements in security and a more relaxed travel status for Borneo. In February, the embassy lowered its travel advisory for eastern Sabah to Level 1, advising Americans to exercise normal precaution.

items.title: Death toll from Nepal-China flash floods at 1,220, nearly 4,800 missing
items.summary: ISLAMABAD: The death toll from last week's devastating flash floods and mudslides on the China-Nepal border has climbed to 1,220, while nearly 4,762 people, including 844 foreigners, remained missing, Anadolu Ajansi reported, citing the latest official data on Wednesday. According to Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, 1,204 bodies have been recovered in Nepal since massive flash floods hit the Himalayan country on August 26, while 301 people were injured and around 4,216 remained missing. A 44-member Korea Disaster Relief Team from South Korea reached Nepal Wednesday to help find the missing people.

items.title: Gold hits 3-week low as Mideast tensions fan rate-hike fears
items.summary: NEW YORK: Gold dropped to a three-week low yesterday as rising Middle East tensions drove up oil prices, stoking inflation and rate-hike fears. US gold futures for December delivery fell one per cent to US$4,350.80. Oil prices rose for a third straight session, while US Treasury yields advanced.

items.title: DoE to step up monitoring to curb activities worsening haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Department of Environment (DoE) will step up monitoring to ensure activities that could worsen the haze do not occur, particularly open burning. He said the DoE had also issued letters to landowners and plantation operators, urging them to play their part in preventing activities that could worsen the Air Pollutant Index (API). Rosli said vehicle movements also contributed to declining air quality.

items.title: Pandu Citra key platform to strengthen public service leadership - Chief secretary
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2026 Pandu Citra Week organised by the National Institute of Public Administration (Intan) serves as an important platform for strengthening leadership within the public service, said Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar. "Be a Pandu Citra ambassador who helps cultivate a culture of guiding, listening to and developing others in the organisation. In addition, Putrajaya Hospital Deputy Director of Medical Dr Mohammad Khairol Anwar Yusop was selected as the 2026 Pandu Citra Sektor Awam ambassador.

items.title: Second suspect arrested after Sri Petaling cable‑theft chase; remanded seven days
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Police have detained another local man to assist in investigations into a cable theft case in Sri Petaling here. Kuala Lumpur Police Chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the 32-year-old man was believed to be the driver of a Ford Ranger which was pursued on Monday from the Awan Besar Toll Plaza heading towards Klang (West) before the chase ended at Jalan Hang Tuah 4. On Monday, a police team fired several shots before detaining a 29-year-old man suspected of cable theft after the Ford Ranger driven by his accomplice attempted to flee a police inspection in Sri Petaling.

items.title: Sunway Lagoon says all injured guests discharged, keeps roller coaster closed pending probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — The roller coaster attraction involved in the August 22, 2026 incident at Sunway Lagoon theme park in Subang Jaya, which is believed to have stopped abruptly after failing to move forward during a ride, remains closed while investigations are ongoing. “Sunway Theme Parks remains firmly committed to maintaining the highest standards of safety and to ensuring the well-being of everyone who visits our parks,” it said. Sunway Theme Parks confirms that all guests who were admitted to the hospital for further observation following the incident have now been discharged.

items.title: SMART prepared for Nepal deployment, with logistics and personnel on standby, says commander
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — The Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) has its personnel and logistics on standby for possible deployment to Nepal. “The SMART team is ready physically and mentally, and prepared for any deployment for this mission. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim previously said SMART would assist in search and rescue (SAR) operations in Nepal following the flood disaster, including locating and bringing home affected Malaysians.

items.title: Perhilitan relocates elephant ‘Sulong Chalil’ to Terengganu Taman Negara after Gerik recapture
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 2 — A wild male elephant known as “Sulong Chalil” has been relocated today to Terengganu Taman Negara through the Tasik Kenyir entrance, a natural forest habitat suitable for wild elephants. The department said that since Aug 17, the Perhilitan team has been closely monitoring Sulong’s movements and physical condition, including the injury recorded on his right leg. “Throughout the operation, Sulong always received monitoring and veterinary treatment.

items.title: Police obtain four‑day remand for boat operator in fatal Mersing collision that left two dead
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 2 — A boat operator involved in the incident where two passenger boats collided in Kuala Sungai Mersing, killing two people last Sunday, has been remanded for four days starting today. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the 33-year-old local man was arrested by a Criminal Investigation Division team of the Mersing district police headquarters (IPD) at about 12 noon yesterday to assist in the investigation. He said the suspect was then taken to the Kota Tinggi Magistrate’s Court for a remand application under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code.

items.title: Former Tabung Haji COO to be charged in Shah Alam Sessions Court tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — A former Lembaga Tabung Haji chief operating officer is expected to be charged at the Shah Alam Sessions Court tomorrow. The Star reported that a court e‑filing entry lists Datuk Adi Azuan Abdul Ghani as scheduled to appear before Sessions Court judge Awang Kerisnada Awang Mahmud at 9am on September 3. The arrests include a former Tabung Haji investment director, the director of Putrajaya Perdana, the former director of Putra Perdana Construction, the former Tabung Haji chairman, the chief executive officer of Alam Maritim and a former federal minister.

items.title: Minister: National Scam Response Centre returned RM5.16m to victims, from funds seized between January and July 2026
items.summary: “For us, the return of money to victims is among the enforcement outcomes that can be directly felt by the people,” he said at a press conference after officiating the 6th International Cyber Resilience Conference (CRC) here today. He said the figures also indicated that cyber threats were becoming increasingly serious, with the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) reporting that scam operations in Southeast Asia alone generated tens of billions of dollars annually. Touching on figures for online sexual abuse, he said cases involving child sexual abuse material (CSAM) increased from 68 in 2024 to 152 last year, while another 100 cases were recorded up to the middle of this year.

items.title: Felda pledges full cooperation as MACC opens six probes into agency, FIC
items.summary: In a statement today, Felda said it fully respected the ongoing investigation process to ensure that it was carried out transparently, fairly and comprehensively. Felda also called on all parties to respect the investigation process. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said today that the commission had opened six new investigation papers into allegations of misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving Felda and its subsidiary, Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC).

items.title: Anwar warns US-Iran hostilities risk wider regional conflict, urges return to diplomacy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today urged the United States (US) and Iran to immediately halt further escalation and return to diplomacy amid renewed hostilities between the two countries. No military objective justifies exposing civilians to an expanding conflict,” he said. “I urge the United States and Iran to halt further escalation and return immediately to diplomacy and the understandings reached in June,” he said.

items.title: Claim on Malaysia recruiting 200,000 Bangladeshi workers not Bangladesh’s official position, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — A statement by a Bangladeshi junior minister claiming that Malaysia planned to recruit 200,000 workers from the country does not represent the official position of the Bangladeshi government, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. He said Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R Ramanan had confirmed that a junior member had made the statement on behalf of the Bangladesh government and that it did not represent the country’s official position. Meanwhile, Fahmi said the Cabinet had been informed that 1,476 Myanmar nationals held at immigration detention depots would be repatriated to their home country at the end of this month.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain to hit KL and 12 states until 7pm, says MetMalaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur and 12 states until 7pm tonight. MetMalaysia in a statement today announced that the bad weather is expected to occur throughout Perlis, Kedah, Terengganu as well as three areas in Penang including Seberang Perai Utara, Seberang Perai Tengah dan Seberang Perai Selatan. Similar warnings have also been issued for Selangor (Hulu Selangor, Gombak and Hulu Langat), Negeri Sembilan (Tampin, Rembau, Jelebu, Seremban, Jempol and Kuala Pilah), and Johor (Segamat).

items.title: Fahmi: Sarawak’s Malaysia Day celebration to be held indoors at BCCK; outdoor events off due to haze
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — Malaysia Day 2026 celebrations on September 16 will be held as scheduled at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK), Sarawak, but outdoor events cannot be held due to the worrying haze situation in Kuching and Serian. Communications Minister and chairman of the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day Celebrations (HKHM) Main Committee Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the decision was made after taking into account the haze situation in both areas. “The Cabinet also took note that the rather worrying haze situation in Kuching and Serian means that outdoor events cannot proceed.

items.title: MACC ready to probe N. Sembilan Pakatan allocation if misuse proven, says commissioner
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is ready to investigate if there is evidence of misuse involving the RM180,000 allocation granted to each Pakatan Harapan (PH) state assemblyman prior to the dissolution of the Negeri Sembilan State Assembly on June 5. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said reports accompanied by evidence showing fund misuse or legal offences would serve as a basis for the commission to initiate an investigation. Meanwhile, in a separate case, Abd Halim said the MACC had yet to receive a letter regarding a corruption case involving former human resources minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan.

items.title: Serian and Kuching record hazardous API levels in Sarawak at 4pm; more areas very unhealthy
items.summary: According to the Malaysian API Management System (APIMS), Kuching recorded a hazardous API reading of 309. Meanwhile, five areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy API readings: Samarahan (287), Sarikei (256), Sibu (248), Sri Aman (247) and Mukah (205). Forty-five stations recorded API readings at the moderate level, while none recorded readings in the good category.

items.title: MACC: Six Felda and FIC cases under investigation, arrests imminent
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has opened six new investigation papers into alleged misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) and its subsidiary, Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC), with several arrests expected beginning next week. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the investigations followed information received on Aug 24 regarding the implementation of projects and investments by Felda and FIC management between 2010 and 2020. The six matters are the purchase of Tataran Aras Sdn Bhd in Limbang, Sarawak; the acquisition of Grand Borneo Hotel Sdn Bhd in Sabah; the purchase of Grand Plaza Serviced Apartments in London; the establishment of Felda Wellness Corporation Sdn Bhd; the acquisition of Felda House and Grand Felda House; and alleged misappropriation in the development of the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project.

items.title: Perak police launch investigations over toddler’s fatal fall at Victoria Bridge
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 2 — Police have opened two investigation papers into the death of a three-year-old boy who is believed to have fallen about five metres from Victoria Bridge in Enggor, near Kuala Kangsar, yesterday. Perak Police Chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the investigation papers were opened under Section 31(1) of the Child Act 2001, with several individuals summoned to assist the investigation. Meanwhile, State Housing and Local Government Committee chairperson Sandrea Ng Shy Ching said the Kuala Kangsar Municipal Council (MPKK) had immediately closed visitor access to the steel structure section of the bridge as a safety measure.

items.title: MACC investigator: Muhyiddin abused powers as PM to help Jana Wibawa contractors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin abused his powers as a prime minister when he acted to help Bumiputera contractors to eventually get government projects under the Jana Wibawa programme, an anti-corruption investigator told the High Court. When asked by Wan Shaharuddin to explain why he said Muhyiddin had abused his powers as prime minister, Mazery said this was due to Muhyiddin’s actions in relation to companies who were applying for Jana Wibawa projects. Muhyiddin was prime minister from March 1, 2020 until Aug 20, 2021.

items.title: Don’t sacrifice independent oversight for speed in Sabah’s water crisis fixes, says former Water Dept director
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 2 — Sabah’s recurring water supply problems require urgent and practical solutions, but the push for faster action should not come at the expense of independent engineering judgement, said Datuk Amarjit Singh. The former Sabah Water Department director said a clear distinction must be maintained between an engineering consultancy practice and a commercial service provider, particularly when companies supplying water infrastructure, equipment, or specialised technologies are also proposing solutions. Amarjit said companies recommending technologies in which they have a commercial interest could face an inherent potential conflict, making independent assessment important.

items.title: Batik Air agrees to resume Miri-KL flights after deputy minister’s request
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 2 — Batik Air has agreed to resume its Miri-Kuala Lumpur services following a formal request by Deputy Minister of Tourism, Arts and Culture Chiew Choon Man. The Miri MP said the commencement date, flight frequency and schedule would be announced by the airline in due course. Chiew said he had received increasing feedback from Miri residents over the difficulty of securing flights between Miri and Kuala Lumpur, particularly during weekends, public holidays and peak travel periods.

items.title: Retiree loses RM1.417m after transferring savings across multiple accounts in phone‑call scam
items.summary: Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the victim, a 66-year-old man, received a call from an unknown individual on May 19 who claimed that the victim was involved in money laundering activities. He said the victim was then instructed to open an Agrobank account and transfer his savings to the account for the purpose of checking by the authorities. “After opening the account, a man came to meet the victim in his residential area and the victim handed over his bank card and PIN number to the man,” he said in a statement.

items.title: US embassy shifts Sabah travel status to ‘relaxed’ after security improvements
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 2 — The United States is encouraging its citizens and international travellers to visit Sabah, citing significant improvements in security and a corresponding relaxation of travel advisories, said US Embassy Kuala Lumpur Chargé d'Affaires David Gamble. Many countries are following America’s lead and reviewing their travel advisories as well,” Gamble said during the launch of the Freedom 250 Sabah programme at the Tanjung Aru State Library today. We want to encourage more tourists to visit Sabah because Sabah is a wonderful place to visit.”

items.title: Johor dengue cases jump 131pc to 9,954 as infections rise across districts
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 2 — Johor recorded 9,954 dengue cases as of Epid Week (ME) 34 this year, an increase of 131.3 per cent compared to 4,304 cases for the same period last year. State Health and Environment Committee Chairman Ling Tian Soon said of the total, 4,520 cases or 45.4 per cent were reported from outbreak localities while 5,434 cases or 54.6 per cent were from non-outbreak localities. “Of the total dengue cases reported throughout ME34, 308 cases or 46.4 per cent were reported from outbreak localities and 356 cases or 53.6 per cent from non-outbreak localities,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: One teen found dead as search continues for three others missing in Tanjung Balau
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 2 — The body of one of four teenagers feared drowned at Tanjung Lompat Beach in Tanjung Balau was recovered this afternoon. The victim, identified as Alif Taqiudin Kamal Hasrul Mohamad, was found by the search and rescue (SAR) team and members of the public at 1.25pm, approximately 800 metres from the location where he was last seen. Kota Tinggi police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohd Syamsuri Mohamad confirmed that the body was identified by family members and has since been transported to Kota Tinggi Hospital.

items.title: MMEA detains tugboat and dredger over suspected ship‑to‑ship transfer; RM260m oil cargo seized off Tanjung Buai
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) detained two vessels suspected of carrying out unauthorised ship-to-ship activities in national waters early yesterday morning, with the value of the seized goods estimated at RM260 million. Tanjung Sedili Zone Maritime acting director Maritime Commander Mohd Najib Sam said the action was carried out at 3.20am after receiving public information regarding two suspicious vessels seen huddled together at a position about 1.4 nautical miles northwest of Tanjung Buai. Mohd Najib said the tugboat was operated by a crew of five including the skipper, consisting of local and Indonesian citizens aged between 26 and 58 years, while the dredger was operated by a crew of 13 including the skipper, all local citizens aged between 22 and 51 years.
